requirement:
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its fenced declaration, including its complete body but excluding anchor option lines, MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
The subject `requirements.authoring_input` has two obligations. The subject's fenced declaration must be in the mandatory input set. It must include the complete body. Anchor option lines must be excluded. The supplied tests cover each of these.

- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` is the key test. It declares a requirement with `:impl:` and `:test:` anchor lines and a multi-line body. The body has a blank line and a body-text line that reads `:impl: this is body text`. It asserts exact equality on the whole input set. The first input is the declaration with the fence lines `:::{req} ready` and `:::` and the full body, including the blank line and the in-body `:impl:` line. The two real anchor option lines are absent. The anchored file then appears as a separate input. This verifies "complete body", "excluding anchor option lines", and that only option lines are stripped, not body text that looks like one. It also asserts that `subject_text` keeps the body.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment]` asserts exact equality on a minimal requirement. The input set is the single declaration with its fences and body, with `matches` set to the subject. It also shows that earlier evidence inputs do not displace it.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` checks the declaration of an example subject. It asserts that the first mandatory input names the subject and that its full text equals the fenced declaration. The same test checks the requirement-subject bundle alongside other contributions.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_inputs_can_read_untracked_declarations_and_terms]` is also marked and exercises the git-tracked and untracked declaration paths.

The obligation to cite `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` is a documentation convention, not behavior to test. The deduplication, resolution and read-denial obligations of `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` belong to that requirement. I did not assess them here.

I found no plausible violation that these assertions would accept. Dropping part of the body, stripping body lines that look like anchors, leaving anchor lines in, or omitting the fence would each fail the exact-equality assertions.
